questions.q: What is Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece in Barcelona, which uses 'hyperboloid' and 'paraboloid' structures to eliminate the need for traditional flying buttresses?
questions.n: This basilica uses ruled geometrical surfaces to transfer loads vertically, creating a self-supporting forest of columns.

questions.q: Gaudí famously used a 'catenary' or 'funicular' model made of hanging chains and weights to design the arches of which project?
questions.n: Gaudí spent ten years developing a 1:10 scale model of chains to find the perfect natural compressive shape for the arches.

questions.q: What is the term for the mosaic technique Gaudí used, where he utilized broken pieces of ceramic tile and glass to cover curved surfaces?
questions.n: Trencadís allowed Gaudí to clothe complex, undulating organic forms with vibrant, weather-resistant recycled materials.

questions.q: Which residential building by Gaudí is nicknamed 'La Pedrera' (The Quarry) due to its undulating stone façade?
questions.n: Its rough-hewn stone appearance and lack of straight lines led locals to compare it to an open quarry.

questions.q: Gaudí’s work is often categorized under which broader architectural movement that was popular in Europe during the late 19th and early 20th centuries?
questions.n: Gaudí was the leading figure of Catalan Modernisme, the regional expression of the organic Art Nouveau movement.

questions.q: What are the distinctive, wing-like wooden carvings that protrude from the front of the Maranao Torogan house?
questions.n: The panolong is a carved end-beam that makes the Torogan look as if it is floating or a ship in motion.

questions.q: What is the name of the traditional Maranao floral/serpent motif carved into the beams and panels of the Torogan?
questions.n: Okir is a design tradition characterized by flowing curvilinear lines and leaf-and-vine patterns.

questions.q: To make the Torogan earthquake-resistant, the massive wooden pillars (postes) are not buried in the ground but are instead placed on top of what?
questions.n: Placing the posts on boulders allows the structure to sway during tremors, preventing the wood from snapping or rotting in soil.

questions.q: Who is the high-ranking social figure or noble intended to live in a Torogan?
questions.n: The Torogan is the communal center and residence for the ruling class of the Maranao people.

questions.q: What is the name of the central beam of the Torogan house, which is often highly decorated?
o: Tinai a Walay (Intestine of the House)
questions.n: This central beam supports the king post and is considered the 'gut' or life-line of the structure.

questions.q: Which Belgian architect is credited with designing the first true Art Nouveau building, the Hôtel Tassel?
questions.n: Horta's use of exposed iron and integrated plant-like ornamentation in 1893 marked the birth of the style.

questions.q: In Art Nouveau ironwork, what is the name of the signature 'whiplash' curve that mimics the movement of a plant stem?
questions.n: This dynamic, asymmetrical line is the most recognizable decorative element of the Art Nouveau movement.

questions.q: Which Austrian movement, led by Otto Wagner and Gustav Klimt, was the Viennese version of Art Nouveau?
questions.n: The Secessionists sought to create a 'Total Art' that broke away from the conservative academic institutions of the time.

questions.q: The Glasgow School of Art is the most famous work of which Scottish Art Nouveau architect?
questions.n: Mackintosh developed a unique 'Glasgow Style' that combined floral Art Nouveau with strong Japanese and geometric influences.

questions.q: What new material was frequently used during the Art Nouveau period to create the intricate, vine-like curves on building facades and entrances?
questions.n: The malleability of iron allowed architects to 'draw' in three dimensions, creating the movement's iconic organic railings and structures.

questions.q: Which architect is associated with the dictum 'Less is a Bore', which became a battle cry for Post-Modernism?
questions.n: Venturi used this phrase to directly challenge the austerity of the International Style in his book 'Complexity and Contradiction'.

questions.q: Who stated that 'A house is a machine for living in'?
questions.n: He believed architecture should be as efficient as a ship or a car, reflecting the industrial progress of the age.

questions.q: The philosophy of 'Organic Architecture' (the idea that a building should grow from its site) is the lifelong theme of which architect?
questions.n: Wright's Fallingwater is the ultimate example of a building that appears to be part of the natural landscape.

questions.q: Who is the architect behind the phrase 'God is in the details'?
questions.n: Mies emphasized that the quality of architecture is found in the meticulous execution of its smallest components.

questions.q: Who famously described architecture as 'Frozen Music'?
questions.n: The German polymath used this metaphor to explain the rhythmic and harmonic nature of structural design.

questions.q: Who designed the Church of the Holy Sacrifice in UP Diliman, the first thin-shell concrete dome in the Philippines?
questions.n: This circular church was a landmark collaboration involving several National Artists and pushed the limits of concrete at the time.

questions.q: Which architect designed the Manila Polo Club and is known for his 'Art Deco' influence in the Far Eastern University (FEU) campus?
questions.n: Antonio’s work on the FEU campus is one of the most significant Art Deco ensembles in Asia.

questions.q: Who designed the Avenue Theater and the State Theater in Manila, and was the first architect to be named a National Artist?
questions.n: Nakpil was a giant of Philippine architecture who adapted modern trends to the local context throughout the 20th century.

questions.q: Which architect designed the National Museum of the Philippines (originally the National Library/Legislative building) and the Manila Post Office?
questions.n: Arellano's Neoclassical masterpieces defined the civic identity of Manila during the American colonial period.

questions.q: Who designed the Our Lady of Peace and Good Voyage (Antipolo Cathedral)?
questions.n: Zaragoza was a master of modern ecclesiastical design, combining modern forms with traditional spiritual needs.
